title: Prehistorica Species Entry Template & Sourcing Guidelines

primaryArtMedia.requirement: Must be clean digital life-reconstruction artwork — a full-body illustration on a plain/transparent or natural backdrop.
prohibitedForPrimaryArt: Skeletal diagrams or anatomical line art
Scans or figures from academic papers / journals
Images with baked-in text, labels, numbers, scale bars, or citation watermarks
Museum exhibit photographs or fossil displays

classificationRules.primaryArt: Clean life reconstruction illustration ONLY -> type: 'art'
classificationRules.skeletalOrTechnicalDiagram: Skeletal drawing, muscle reconstruction, or technical anatomical diagram -> type: 'diagram' or 'scale_diagram'
classificationRules.fossilSpecimenPhoto: Actual fossil bone photo, museum specimen photograph -> type: 'photo'

speciesTemplate.name: Exampleosaurus
speciesTemplate.dietDetails: Apex predator feeding on herbivorous dinosaurs in floodplains.
speciesTemplate.sizeNotes: Length based on complete holotype specimen FMNH PR2081.
speciesTemplate.discoveryHistory:
• First discovered in 1902 by Barnum Brown in Montana.
• Named in 1905 by Henry Fairfield Osborn.
• Multiple well-preserved skeletons recovered across North America.
interestingFacts: Possessed one of the strongest bite forces of any terrestrial carnivore.
Had highly developed olfactory bulbs for smelling prey across vast distances.
Reached full adult size in approximately 20 years.

sources.citation: Osborn, H. F. (1905). Tyrannosaurus and other Cretaceous carnivorous dinosaurs. Bulletin of the AMNH.
